text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pioneering the drive to build more low and low-medium-cost houses, 26 developers committed themselves in writing to construct 47,000 such units in Penang.
- Malaysia has proposed that an international body other than the World Trade Organisation (WTO) deal with non-trade issues so as to enable the WTO to concentrate on the trade and investment issues.

- The government has asked fast-food giant KFC Holdings to ease its franchising requirements so that small businessmen can open KFC outlets for less than 250,000 ringgit, about one-sixth of the current minimum.

- Two opposition party state assemblymen quit the party to join the Malaysian Chinese Association on Tuesday. With the cross-over, the National Front party has gained complete control of the Negri Sembilan state assembly.

- An Umno (United Malays National Organisation) branch chief was found dead with his throat slit with his wife lying next to him with serious head and facial injuries in their home in the east coast town of Kuantan on Tuesday afternoon.
